decisions.reason: The current journal source (Campbell, Ergun, Jackson, & Kim, 2021; 10.1080/23279095.2021.1917411) consists of the published abstract and publisher-deposited Crossref reference array; the 2019/2020 Campbell dissertation is a distinct work and context only. In the journal abstract, the sole target study is explicitly described as 'a systematic replication of a study conducted by Jones et al. using a demographically-different sample of participants,' testing the correlation between NAART error scores and WRAT4 Word Reading raw scores, comparing WRAT4 WR raw-score distributions, and applying Jones et al.'s original regression equation to predict fourth- and fifth-grade reading-level classifications. Deposited reference CIT0011 in the current journal metadata carries DOI 10.1080/09084282.2011.643966, which is Jones, Proto, Musso, Barker, and Gouvier (2012), 'Using the NAART to Estimate WRAT-4 Reading Grade Level in a Predominantly African American Sample' (also corroborated by the dissertation context). Because this exact target is already represented by shipped row 780, candidate target 0 is not a missing row.

In the current 2021 journal abstract, the authors explicitly state that the project was a systematic replication of a study conducted by Jones et al. using a demographically different sample of participants, testing the original NAART regression equation to predict WRAT4 reading grade-level classification. Both the shipped row and blind target 0 rightly code the record type as a replication.

corrected_value.title: Using the NAART to Estimate WRAT-4 Reading Grade Level in a Predominantly African American Sample

decisions.reason: The current 2021 journal abstract identifies the target as 'a study conducted by Jones et al.' whose regression equation uses the NAART to predict WRAT4 reading grade-level classification. In the publisher-deposited reference list for this same 2021 journal article, entry CIT0011 provides the exact DOI 10.1080/09084282.2011.643966, which bibliography_metadata.json resolves to Jones, Proto, Musso, Barker, and Gouvier (2012), 'Using the NAART to Estimate WRAT-4 Reading Grade Level in a Predominantly African American Sample' (also corroborated as context by the related dissertation). Shipped row 780 is complete and exact.

Evaluated strictly from the available current 2021 journal evidence (abstract plus deposited references; journal full text remains unavailable), NAART error scores and WRAT4 WR raw scores were significantly correlated, predicted versus actual reading-level proportions at/above or below 4th and 5th grade did not significantly differ, and the authors explicitly conclude that the original Jones et al. (2012) regression equation accurately predicts reading level classification in the current sample (with raw-score distribution differences reflecting sample demographics rather than replication failure). Although the separate 2019/2020 dissertation context additionally reports Cohen's kappa (.00 at 4th grade, .78 at 5th grade), per the quality gate the thesis is a distinct work and context only and cannot transfer unverified body statistics or override the journal abstract's explicit overall successful verdict.
